header:
Market vs limit:
speed or price?

lines.text: In 2010, a $40 stock sold for one penny.
lines.say: In twenty ten, a forty dollar stock sold for one penny.

lines.text: It was Accenture, in the May 6, 2010 flash crash. The order type mattered.
lines.say: It was Accenture, during the May sixth, twenty ten flash crash, and the type of order mattered.

lines.text: A market order says: buy or sell now, at the best price available.
lines.say: A market order says, buy or sell right now, at the best price available.

lines.text: A limit order says: only at my price or better.
lines.say: A limit order says, only at my price, or better.

lines.text: Say a stock is offered at $50.10 and you buy 100 shares. That's $5,010.
lines.say: Say a stock is offered at fifty dollars and ten cents, and you buy a hundred shares. That's five thousand and ten dollars.

lines.text: If it jumps to $51 before a market order fills, you pay $5,100. That's $90 more.
lines.say: If it jumps to fifty-one dollars before a market order fills, you pay fifty-one hundred. That's ninety dollars more.

lines.text: The limit order pays at most $5,010, but it might not fill at all.
lines.say: The limit order pays at most five thousand and ten, but it might not fill at all.

lines.text: In 2010, over 20,000 trades hit prices 60% or more off, and exchanges and FINRA canceled them.
lines.say: Back in twenty ten, over twenty thousand trades hit prices sixty percent or more off, and exchanges and FINRA canceled them.

lines.text: The takeaway: market orders buy speed. Limit orders buy control over price.
lines.say: The takeaway? Market orders buy speed. Limit orders buy control over price.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Market vs limit orders: the day a $40 stock traded for 1¢
post.ig:
In 2010, a $40 stock sold for one penny.

In the May 6, 2010 flash crash, Accenture traded as low as $0.01 before closing at $41.09.
A market order fills now at the best available price, which isn't guaranteed. A limit order fills only at your price or better, but might not fill.
Over 20,000 trades 60%+ off their 2:40 p.m. prices were canceled.

Sources: SEC investor bulletin on order types, SEC-CFTC report (Sept 2010).
News and education, not financial advice.
